title: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and cheese is a dish of boiled pasta tossed in a rich sauce made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, garlic and aromatic herbs, finished with grated cheese (usually Parmesan or mozzarella). It is a staple of Mediterranean cuisine and often served as a quick lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce is the foundation of many Italian dishes, including pasta, pizza and ragù.
Tomatoes are high in lycopene, a red pigment with strong antioxidant properties.
Traditionally pasta is cooked “al dente” to retain a pleasant bite.
Cheese not only adds flavor but also improves calcium absorption from the tomatoes.
The dish can be easily adapted for dietary needs: gluten‑free pasta, vegan cheese or reduced‑salt versions.

items.title: Rich source of lycopene
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes has antioxidant effects and may support heart health and reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Provides complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta supplies steady energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Calcium and protein from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium for bone health and protein for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and pasta contain B1, B3 and B6 vitamins, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats from olive oil
items.content: Olive oil in the sauce provides monounsaturated fats that support vascular health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese can be high in salt; people with hypertension should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Cheese contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional wheat pasta contains gluten; those with celiac disease need a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato products.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossing it with the sauce so every strand is coated. Sprinkle with grated cheese and fresh basil or oregano. Optional additions include olives, capers, or sautéed vegetables for extra flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Sauce can be frozen in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Keep dry pasta in a cool, dry place away from moisture.
